comparator.name: English Language and Culture
comparator.route: Balanced electives with a linguistics final project
comparator.sourceNotes: The September 2026 intake follows the redesigned 180 EC degree. Year 1 is shared. The selected second and third years each use two electives in block 2A and two in block 2B. This example uses the 10 EC Portfolio or BA Thesis course and meets the published linguistics entry requirements through courses completed in year two.

alternatives.label: Literature, language & Anglophone cultures
alternatives.concept: Study how stories and language shape identity across literary texts, public speech and media. Combine close reading with stylistics, psycholinguistics, historical research and cultural analysis.
alternatives.labelReason: Literary interpretation, rhetoric, stylistics and psycholinguistics provide a broad response, with Anglophone and transatlantic examples in literature, film and history.
progression: Introductory literary study, rhetoric and brain and behaviour precede stylistics and psycholinguistics. Later literary theory, qualitative methods and media analysis lead to rhetorical practice and historical research.

alternatives.label: Literature, culture & media
alternatives.concept: Explore how literature and film represent identity, empire and cultural memory. Develop close reading and literary theory alongside media analysis, history and the interpretation of art and heritage.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum centres literary study but substantially extends it through film, media, cultural history, heritage and art-historical interpretation.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the balanced closest match, this route removes psycholinguistics and most advanced rhetoric and social theory in favour of archaeology, gender history, media archaeology, empire, art, museums and heritage.
progression: Literary and film foundations and introductory history precede advanced work in adaptation, representation, documentary and historical interpretation. Methods work precedes final research-oriented cultural study.

alternatives.label: Language, rhetoric & cognition
alternatives.concept: Study how people acquire, process and use language. Connect stylistics and rhetoric with psycholinguistics and cognition, and use qualitative inquiry to examine communication in social settings.
alternatives.labelReason: The curriculum does not reproduce a formal English-linguistics major, but its strongest organising thread is language use and rhetoric supported by cognitive, philosophical and social inquiry.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the balanced and literature-media routes, this curriculum gives greater weight to psycholinguistics, cognition, rhetoric, persuasion, philosophy of mind and emotion, and advanced research while retaining a smaller literary-cultural foundation.
progression: Introductory rhetoric and brain and behaviour precede stylistics, applied rhetoric and psycholinguistics. Qualitative inquiry supports later work on public communication and representation, while higher cognition precedes final research synthesis.

candidates.label: English linguistics, language in society and cognition

routeSelection.route: Balanced electives with a linguistics final project
routeSelection.basis: This representative sequence retains literature, linguistics, professional writing and global culture. The second-year linguistics selections provide entry to the final project while preserving literature electives in both years.

selection.assessment: After the balanced closest match, two generator-backed and feasible directions remain materially distinct: literature, culture and media; and language, rhetoric and cognition. Both meet the pairwise distinctness threshold, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

blocks: Both develop close reading and literary interpretation across texts and genres.
Both analyse how narratives construct personal and cultural identities.
Both use critical theory to interpret literature. Groningen’s selected course focuses on human rights.
Groningen has a dedicated medieval English literature course.
Groningen studies English-language literary traditions shaped by colonial histories.
Groningen traces changes in the literary imagination across Anglophone history.
Style & Meaning studies how linguistic choices produce meaning in social and textual contexts.
Psycholinguistics supplies the closest UCR study of cognitive language processing and development.
Both develop structured argument and public speaking. Groningen also teaches academic English and literary essay writing.
Groningen develops writing and editorial skills for popular genres.
Groningen teaches conversation analysis and language as joint action.
Both examine how mediated stories shape social identities and cultural understanding.
This option uses interdisciplinary teamwork to study complex problems and public responses.
Both develop evidence-based argument, written expression and accurate source use. Groningen applies these skills to English language study.
Groningen requires an individual project, with a portfolio or thesis route. UCR’s optional 15 EC research element sits outside the course schedule.

notes.text: Groningen offers a dedicated sequence in English linguistics, literary history and professional English, with a final project in the subject. The UCR options combine related work in literature, media, rhetoric and cognition.

audience.programmeDescription: Groningen studies English-language literatures, language and cultures from the medieval period to the present. This example combines literary study with preparation for a linguistics final project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The UCR options emphasise literature and language, literature and media, or language and cognition.
